title: VE 906 Leitstellen IT-Infrastruktur
description: Die Integrierte Leitstelle Rems-Murr (ILS) und die Integrierte Regionalleitstelle Ostwürttemberg (IRLS) werden die beiden Leitstellen zukünftig als Partnerleitstellen so betreiben, dass die Leitstellen im Regelbetrieb eng zusammenarbeiten und sich gegenseitig unterstützen. Im Falle eines Ausfalls eines Standortes sollen beide Leitstellen von einem Standort aus betrieben werden. Dazu wird entsprechende Leitstellen-IT-Infrastruktur beschafft, so dass die Leitstellen zukünftig in einem Verbund arbeiten. Die Leistung umfasst dabei für beide Standorte • das IT-Virtualisierungssystem zum Betrieb der Leitstellen-Einsatzleitsoftware COBRA des Herstellers ISE zur Notrufbearbeitung, Telekommunikation und Funk-Vermittlung und dessen Schnittstellen. • IT-Sicherheitsinfrastruktur • die dazu notwendige Netzwerkinfrastruktur, bestehend aus Netzwerken und Netzwerkmanagement, inkl. Monitoring • Integration von Verschlüsselungskomponenten • Gebäudetechnikintegration • Schnittstellen zu verschiedenen externen Systemen (RTT, AML, BMA, DA, KMS, etc.) • und die zugehörigen Projektdienstleistungen. Der Leistungsumfang des Auftragnehmers (AN) umfasst die Bereitstellung der für die jeweiligen Systeme erforderlichen Software- und Hardwarekomponenten sowie die Sicherstellung der vollständigen Funktionsfähigkeit der Schnittstellen untereinander. Der AN erbringt neben dem Aufbau der Systeme explizit auch die Leistung eines Systemintegrators. Seine Aufgabe ist die Integration des eigenen Systems und der für dieses Projekt beigestellten, über Schnittstellen verbundenen Systeme und weiterer Einrichtungen des AG. Hauptmassen: Virtualisierungsserver / Firewalls / Netzwerkkomponenten /Arbeitsplatzrechner

title: Denmark – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Totalrådgiverkontrakt - Projektet vedr. etablering af cykelsti, Nordfyns Kommune
description: Nordfyns Kommune ønsker at udførselsfasen skal bydes ud i hovedentreprise. Nærværende udbud omfatter projektering og udførelse af en ny cykelsti mellem Særslev og Bogense. Der skal i projektet bl.a. arbejdes med trafiksikkerhed, dobbeltrettet cykelsti, evt. enkeltrettet cykelsti, afvanding, belysning. Der henvises til pkt. 1 og 2 i Totalrådgiverkontrakten samt de herinævnte bilag, herunder særligt projektbeskrivelsen bilag F1 og ansøgningen til vejdirektoratet Totalrådgiverens ydelser omfatter, men er ikke begrænset til: Der skal i udformningen af projektet lægges vægt på alle miljømæssige forhold i relation til anlægsarbejdet og landskabet, ikke mindst i relation til den fremtidige drift. Der udarbejdes komplet materiale inkl. udbudsmateriale til hovedentreprisen samt varetagelse af byggeledelse, sikkerhedskoordinering og fagtilsyn i udførelsesfasen iht. nedenstående punkter og Ydelsesbeskrivelser for anlæg 2019 jf. bilag F2 og F4. • 1. – Indledende rådgivning • 2. – Projekteringsledelse • 3. – Forslag • 4. - Myndighedsprojekt • 5. – Udbudsprojekt • 6. - Udførelsesprojekt • 7. – Udførelse (byggeledelse, fagtilsyn, projektopfølgning) • 8. - Aflevering • 9. – Andre ydelser (IKT, Forundersøgelser og planlægning, interessenter og brugere, bæredygtighed, arbejdsmiljø, tilgængelighed, Som udført, bistand ifm. idriftsætning, eftersyn) Der henvises til pkt. 2 og 3 i Totalrådgiverkontrakten samt de herinævnte bilag, herunder særligt skema til afgrænsning af rådgiverydelser, bilag F2

TRM Technologies Inc. *** Financial Consumer Agency of Canada (FCAC) thanks you for your interest in our procurement process. The RFP will only be open to the fifteen (15) suppliers listed on the NPP and we will not be adding any additional suppliers to this solicitation. FCAC has met the mandatory requirements under the PSPC SBIPS SA and we are confident that we will be receiving a sufficient number of proposals to make this a truly competitive process. With our current staffing limitations, we cannot invite additional proponents without creating undo process or inefficiencies within our procurement system. FCAC thanks you again for your interest and going forward we will keep your firm in mind for our future requirements. Description of Work: The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada requires the services of an experienced, reputable, and independent third-party cybersecurity firm to conduct an enterprise-level assessment of FCAC’s cybersecurity posture. The assessment shall include an internal evaluation of FCAC’s information technology security controls using ITSG-33 Annex 3A and a harmonized threat and risk assessment methodology, supported by evidence collection, gap analysis, residual risk determination, and prioritized remediation planning. The assessment shall also include a separate National Institute of Standards and Technology Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 report to present FCAC’s cybersecurity posture in a broader, executive-level and externally consumable manner. The internal report shall be detailed, evidence-based, and suitable for management decision-making, while the external report shall provide a high-level maturity narrative suitable for publication or broader stakeholder communication, without disclosing sensitive technical vulnerabilities, system-specific weaknesses, or protected information. title: Safety Vocational Training - H2S Alive and Confined Space
description: Safety Vocational Training - H2S Alive and Confined Space This requirement is for: The Correctional Service of Canada, CORCAN Prairie Region. Trade agreement: This procurement is not subject to any trade agreement. Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: This solicitation is open only to Canadian suppliers. Competitive Procurement Strategy: lowest priced compliant bid. Set-aside under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business: This procurement is open to both Indigenous and non-Indigenous businesses. All interested suppliers may participate. However, suppliers are to note that this requirement is subject to a preference for Indigenous suppliers and will be set-aside under the federal government Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB) if Canada receives two or more responsive bids from Indigenous businesses who meet the requirements of the PSIB. Indigenous businesses that have not already registered in the Indigenous Services Canada (ISC) Indigenous Business Directory should do so. Additional information on the Indigenous Business Directory is available at the following link: https://www.sac-isc.gc.ca/eng/1100100033057/1610797769658#c3. Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement: This procurement is not subject to a Comprehensive Land Claims Agreement. Security Requirements: This contract includes security requirements. Nature of Requirements: The following is a summary of the statement of work for this requirement. The Correctional Service of Canada has a requirement to facilitate reintegration of offenders to the community that includes supporting opportunities for obtaining employment, by providing vocational training programs. It is important to ensure that vocational training recognized by third parties leads to certifications and is relevant to the labour market and community employment. Objectives: To provide, upon request, the following Vocational Safety Training programs leading to certification to groups of offenders at the CSC institutions listed in the Locations of Work. 1) H2S Alive 2) Confined Space Upon successful completion of the training, the Contractor must provide certificates to the successful participants. CORCAN may request that the Contractor deliver the safety courses separately, at different times, due to operational requirements at the site. Deliverables: For all training within the identified course programs, the Contractor must provide: a) Sufficient resources (instructor(s)) to deliver in-class training for each of the CSC institutions listed in the Location of Work based on each institution’s needs, as requested by CSC. b) Training materials, written, practical exercises and testing as required for the completion of the applicable course. c) A comprehensive equipment and tool list to the Project Authority or delegated Manager two (2) weeks in advance of the program start date by email. d) All materials and equipment required for each program, including but not limited to manuals, handouts, training materials, Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), and any other required equipment. e) A list of successful participants to the delegated Manager. f) A copy of certificates for successful participants within 21 days of course completion to the Project Authority by email, as well as the dates of training, the location of training and number of participants. For each course, CORCAN will provide: a) Selection of participants with a confirmed number of participants for the course to the Contractor two (2) working days prior to the course commencement date. b) Facilities for training delivery, including classroom and any equipment required for use during classroom instruction. The Project Authority must pre-approve all types of media utilized for delivery of the training. c) At each training location, sufficient space for practical training. d) At each training location, where available, sufficient storage space and access (depending on site protocols) to store all the Contractor’s materials and equipment required for the duration of each course. e) The CORCAN Project Authority will provide the Contractor with the names of participants for each training session. If the Contractor requires any additional information for certification or registration, the Contractor must collect such additional information directly from the participant. CORCAN will advise participants in advance that the Contractor may request additional information. f) The CORCAN Project Authority will provide a list to the Contractor of the delegated Managers for each CSC institutional location upon award of the Contract. g) The Project Authority or delegated Manager for each CSC institutional location will work with the Contractor to determine course delivery dates. 1.5 Location of work a) The Contractor must perform the work at various CSC Institutions, or Community locations as identified below. title: Request for Offers for the provision of Cleaning Services for the Embassy of Canada to Lebanon, in Beirut
description: The cleaning services must be delivered at The Canadian Embassy to Lebanon, in Beirut. The work includes the provision of routine and periodic cleaning services, as well as any additional cleaning required to meet operational needs. Services must be provided in accordance with the specifications outlined in this Statement of Work and must support a clean, safe, and professional environment at all times while not interfering with the daily operations or activities of the building’s occupants, clients, or visitors. The Canadian Embassy in Beirut, Lebanon is in Spark Tower Bldg, 2415 Sin El Fil, Beirut, Lebanon, a business centre comprising 18 Floors. The total surface area occupied by the embassy is of 3550 m2 and comprises: part of the Ground Floor, the Fourteenth floor, the Fifteenth floor, the Sixteenth floor, the Mezzanine in the Sixteenth floor, the Seventeenth floor, parking spaces, storage rooms, guards and drivers’ rooms. While the majority of the work will be located at the Chancery Building of the Embassy located in Sin El Fil, cleaning staff may be called upon to provide similar work at the Official Residence of the Ambassador or at the apartments of the Embassy’s diplomatic staff in Ashrafieh, or at any other venue as required by the Embassy of Canada. Periodical cleaning of the exterior windows of staff quarters may be required and will be paid following an offer and at the submission of an invoice. The pricing will be quoted per occurrences and must be approved by the contracting authority before work starts.

description: Please note that late submissions will not be considered or accepted. This is Phase One of a two-phase process. Phase One will assess interested suppliers' qualifications. In Phase Two, qualified suppliers will be invited to submit financial bids based on the specifications and drawings. The Work consists of exterior storm sewer repairs at the National Forestry Centre (NRCan), including pavement removal, excavation, erosion control, eight catch basin maintenance holes, 229 m of PVC piping, connections to existing pipes, underground power line crossings, inspection and cleaning of 220 m of existing piping, and pavement restoration. The Work also includes a raised pavement area at the gate, repainting 208 parking stalls and six accessible stalls with associated markings, mobilization, demobilization and site cleanup. The Contractor must complete the Work within 17 weeks of notification of acceptance of the offer. This is a secured facility. Contractor personnel must be escorted on site at all times by NRCan and/or Commissionaires. title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Sanierung Werra Sport- und Freizeitbad in D-98646 Hildburghausen - Generalplanung nach §§ 34, 51, 55 HOAI 2021 sowie Besondere Leistungen
description: Das Werra Sport- und Freizeitbad in Hildburghausen ist seit der Errichtung und Einweihung im Jahr 2000 ein zentraler und wichtiger Bestandteil der regionalen Infrastruktur, da es eine unverzichtbare Funktion in den Bereichen Sport, Bildung, Freizeit und Gesundheit erfüllt. Im Besonderen ist hier die Funktion für die Schwimmausbildung im Rahmen des Schulschwimmens für den kompletten Landkreises Hildburghausen zu nennen. Als Ganzjahresbad mit einer Kombination aus Hallen- und Freibadbereich sichert es die Schwimmausbildung für Schulen und Vereine in der Region und dient als wichtige Trainingsstätte für den lokalen Sport. Die große Badelandschaft mit 25 m-Bahnen und Sprungturm ist essenziell für die allgemeine Fitness und das sportliche Training. Darüber hinaus ist das Bad ein beliebtes regionales Ausflugsziel und ein wichtiger sozialer Treffpunkt. Mit Attraktionen wie der 50 m-Riesenrutsche, einem Spaßbecken mit Massagedüsen und einem separaten Kinderplanschbecken bietet es einen wetterunabhängigen Anziehungspunkt für Familien und Erholungssuchende aus dem gesamten Landkreis. Ergänzt wird dieses Angebot durch eine Saunalandschaft, die den Aspekt Wellness und Gesundheitsförderung abdeckt. Zusammenfassend lässt sich sagen, dass das Werra Sport- und Freizeitbad weit über die Funktion eines einfachen Schwimmbades hinausgeht: Es steigert die Lebensqualität der Bürger und bildet eine tragende Säule der Freizeit- und Sportinfrastruktur in Hildburghausen und Süddthüringen. Während die lange diskutierte und komplexe Sanierung des Freibadbereiches im Jahr 2024 abgeschlossen werden konnte, steht nun die umfassende Ertüchtigung der Schwimmhalle selbst an. Trotz einer kleineren Sanierung der Halle im Jahr 2018 sind die technischen Anlagen, die Gebäudehülle und die Innenbereiche nach über zwei Jahrzehnten intensiver Nutzung in einem Zustand, der eine Generalüberholung notwendig macht. Diese Sanierung muss deutlich über kosmetische Reparaturen hinausgehen und die technische, energetische und gestalterische Modernisierung der gesamten Halle sowie der angeschlossenen Saunalandschaft umfassen. Ziel ist es, den Energieverbrauch langfristig zu senken und das Bad zukunftsfähig zu machen. Die Sanierung des Werra Sport- und Freizeitbades ist eine komplexe und anspruchsvolle Planungsaufgabe, für die ein kompetentes Planerteam gesucht wird. Die Brutto-Grundfläche des Gebäudes (BGF) beträgt ca. 3.600 m2. Die Wasserfläche umfasst ca. 480 m2. Für die geplante Maßnahme werden Baukosten von ca. 4,0 Mio Euro (Brutto, KG 300 und 400) veranschlagt.

title: Body, Retainer, and Gasket
description: General Information This is a solicitation for non-commercial products prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR)/Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 13 as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Naval Surface Warfare Center Indian Head Division (NSWC IHD), located in Indian Head, Maryland, intends to award a firm-fixed-price (FFP) purchase order using Simplified Acquisition Procedures for Body, Retainer, and Gasket parts. This solicitation will be competed as a total small business set-aside. Solicitation Details Quotes are being requested under Request for Quotations (RFQ) N0017426Q1120. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 332710 and the associated small business size standard is 500 employees. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through the FAR/RFO. This RFQ incorporates all provisions and clauses in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01 and the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) DPN 20260507. Technical Drawings If interested, technical drawings need to be requested by contractor prior to submission date. ITAR certification is required to be provided prior to technical drawing release. Drawing requests must be made via email to deanna.l.wilson27.civ@us.navy.mil by Friday, 23 October 2026, 10:00 AM EST. Drawings will be send via DoD Safe. Cybersecurity Compliance Requirement (CMMC Level 1): For purposes of technically acceptability, the Offeror shall submit documentation verifying an active CMMC Level 1 Self-Assessment recorded in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS). If the Offeror does not possess an active SPRS entry at the time of proposal submission, the Offeror will not be deemed technically acceptable. Basis for Award The Government will award a purchase order resulting from this solicitation to the responsible vendor whose quote conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The Government intends to evaluate all timely quotes received from eligible vendors on a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) basis. The Government intends to evaluate quotations and award a purchase order without discussion. Evaluation Factors: Technical: Quotes must reflect the required specifications and the exact brand specified in the Statement of Work. Price: Quotes must include all applicable costs, including shipping and handling. Questions and Clarifications Questions regarding this requirement must be submitted via email to deanna.l.wilson27.civ@us.navy.mil no later than Friday, 16 October 2026. All answers will be provided by Friday, 23 October 2026. Submission Instructions Quote packages are due by November 6th, 2026, at 10:00 AM EST. Late quotes will not be considered. Quote packages shall be sent via email to deanna.l.wilson27.civ@us.navy.mil and must contain a cover sheet that provides the following information: Official Company Name; Point of Contact (including name, email address, and phone number); and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and CAGE Code.

title: JP Murtha Float Mooring Bitts Retrofit
description: JP Murtha Float Mooring Bitts Retrofit - The United States Army Corps of Engineers, (USACE) Pittsburgh District has a requirement for the retrofitting of existing hydraulic structures within an active navigation lock. The Prime Contractor must be capable of executing complex in-the-wet construction, specifically: The John P. Murtha Floating Mooring Bitt Retrofit consists of the installation of Government furnished Floating Mooring Bitts into Contractor fabricated embedded frame on the existing River Chamber Middle Wall. In-the-wet construction methods are required. Design, fabrication, and installation of two dewatering boxes are required for installation of the Floating Mooring Bitts. Removal or alterations to existing work in such a manner as to prevent injury or damage to any portions of the existing work which remain. Repair or replace portions of existing work which have been altered during construction operations to match existing or adjoining work, as approved by the Contracting Officer. At the completion of operations, existing work must be in a condition equal to or better than that which existed before new work started. To achieve this Requirement the Contractor must: a. Floating Plant Operations: Providing, operating, and mooring a fully compliant floating plant (crane/deck barge and push boat) in an active river chamber in accordance with EM 385-1-1. b. Dewatering Box (Cofferdam): Fabricating, installing, and sealing structural steel dewatering boxes against lock monoliths for a strict maximum duration of 90 days. c. Heavy Demolition and Concrete Work: Executing concrete wire-sawing, core drilling, and demolition of existing lock wall recesses, followed by cast-in-place concrete integration. d. Structural Steel and Mooring Bitts: Fabricating heavy steel embedded anchorage frames, and salvaging/installing Government-Furnished Floating Mooring Bitts. e. Commercial Diving: Providing certified commercial dive teams to support underwater inspection, rigging, and cofferdam sealing. The work shall be completed within 730 calendar days after written Notice to Proceed. This acquisition will be procured as an Unrestricted Full and Open Solicitation. The resulting award will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Construction Contract. All responsible Bidders are encouraged to participate. description: JP Murtha Float Mooring Bitts Retrofit - The United States Army Corps of Engineers, (USACE) Pittsburgh District has a requirement for the retrofitting of existing hydraulic structures within an active navigation lock. The Prime Contractor must be capable of executing complex in-the-wet construction, specifically: The John P. Murtha Floating Mooring Bitt Retrofit consists of the installation of Government furnished Floating Mooring Bitts into Contractor fabricated embedded frame on the existing River Chamber Middle Wall. In-the-wet construction methods are required. Design, fabrication, and installation of two dewatering boxes are required for installation of the Floating Mooring Bitts. Removal or alterations to existing work in such a manner as to prevent injury or damage to any portions of the existing work which remain. Repair or replace portions of existing work which have been altered during construction operations to match existing or adjoining work, as approved by the Contracting Officer. At the completion of operations, existing work must be in a condition equal to or better than that which existed before new work started. To achieve this Requirement the Contractor must: a. Floating Plant Operations: Providing, operating, and mooring a fully compliant floating plant (crane/deck barge and push boat) in an active river chamber in accordance with EM 385-1-1. b. Dewatering Box (Cofferdam): Fabricating, installing, and sealing structural steel dewatering boxes against lock monoliths for a strict maximum duration of 90 days. c. Heavy Demolition and Concrete Work: Executing concrete wire-sawing, core drilling, and demolition of existing lock wall recesses, followed by cast-in-place concrete integration. d. Structural Steel and Mooring Bitts: Fabricating heavy steel embedded anchorage frames, and salvaging/installing Government-Furnished Floating Mooring Bitts. e. Commercial Diving: Providing certified commercial dive teams to support underwater inspection, rigging, and cofferdam sealing. The work shall be completed within 730 calendar days after written Notice to Proceed. This acquisition will be procured as an Unrestricted Full and Open Solicitation. The resulting award will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Construction Contract. All responsible Bidders are encouraged to participate. title: Request for Information (RFI) - CONUS Generator Maintenance
description: Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Request for Information (RFI) Continental United States locations (CONUS) Generator Maintenance 10/15/2026 The Department of Homeland Security, Federal Emergency Management Agency, Logistics Management Directorate, is conducting market research to identify contractors capable of providing on-site generator maintenance and testing services at four Continental United States locations (CONUS). description: Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) is asking interested parties to provide information for a potential lease of space that meets the following criteria: Section A: Lease Components • a lease term of approximately 10 years, commencing on or about October 1, 2029, with a right of early termination anytime on or after October 1, 2037 provided written notice is given at least 12 months prior, plus option to extend the lease for one (1) additional period of two (2) years; • approximately 1,451 usable square metres (um2) of contiguous office space; • the proposed space must be available approximately 37 weeks prior to the above-noted lease commencement date so all space(s) may be prepared for occupancy; • the proposed space should satisfy or be capable of satisfying the following criteria: 1. a minimum of 665 um2 of the proposed space must be located on the main floor; preference may be given to spaces with any or all of the following: a highly visible storefront space, on a main road, with direct pedestrian access from the street; 2. the proposed space should be within an office or commercial type building; buildings situated within heavy or medium industrial zoning and industrial type buildings with warehouse or manufacturing space will not be considered. A mixed use building may be considered at the sole discretion of PSPC; 3. a dedicated telecommunication/equipment room measuring no less than 20 um2 within the proposed space must be provided; this will not form part of the Lessee's usable area noted above but will be included in the rentable area calculation; 4. parking for approximately 10 vehicles must be available to the public within a one (1) block radius of the proposed space; 5. cleaning services will be required during business hours; 6. have acceptable space for the installation of a bicycle rack; 7. fully accessible to persons with a disability; 8. a public transit stop must be within 600 metres of the building main entrance, and the frequency of service must not be greater than 30 minute intervals between the hours of 0700 hours and 1800 hours, Monday to Friday inclusive; there must be an accessible walking route between the public transit stop and the building; 9. the physical characteristics of the lands and the building and the area and the environment surrounding it, including neighbouring land uses, shall be compatible with the Lessee’s intended use of the accommodation; 10. the dimensions of the proposed space must be compatible for efficient design and use. • the proposed space must be located in the city of Calgary and within the following boundaries (the geographical boundaries include sites on either side of the roads): North: Country Hills Blvd NW, 112 Ave NW, Sarcee Trail NW,144 Avenue NW, South: 16 Ave NW (HWY 1) East: Symons Valley Rd NW, Stoney Trail (201), Shaganappi Trail NW, John Laurie Blvd NW, Brisbois Dr NW, Crowchild Trail NW (HWY 1A) West: Mile Coulee Road, Crowchild Trail NW (HWY 1A), Stoney Trail (201) In the event of any discrepancy between the attached map and text description of the geographic boundaries, the text description shall prevail. This map is to be used for presentation purposes only and is not a legal document • on or before the lease commencement date, the proposed space will have to comply with all requirements contained in PSPC’s Standards for Leased Accommodation, a copy of which may be obtained from the contact listed in Section F; Note: PSPC may wish to visit or inspect the proposed space upon reasonable notice and a threat and risk assessment may be undertaken in order to assess potential threats to the security of the proposed space and to the public.

In the event of unforeseen technical issues, the virtual session may be cancelled. If that happens, presentation materials will be provided to registered attendees following the event. BACKGROUND Let�s Talk About What�s Next. Good acquisition starts with communication. Not just when a solicitation hits SAM.gov. Not just when proposals are due. And certainly not only after we already know exactly what we want to buy. Sometimes the most valuable conversation happens much earlier. On 19 November 2026, Portfolio Acquisition Executive Marine Corps (PAE MC) and Headquarters Marine Corps Installations & Logistics (HQMC I&L) invite industry to join us for our next quarterly Marine Corps Acquisition Exchange (MCAX). Together with the Portfolio Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS) Information Technology Contracting Center (ITCC) and other Marine Corps acquisition and requirements stakeholders, we want to give industry a clearer look at where we're headed�and an opportunity to talk with the people helping us get there. The 19 November MCAX will provide industry with visibility into anticipated contracting opportunities across participating Marine Corps organizations, while creating dedicated time for questions and direct Government�Industry engagement. What are we looking for? Ideas. Capabilities. Competition. Innovation. And, most importantly, meaningful dialogue with industry partners who understand that supporting the Marine Corps begins with understanding the mission. Our senior leaders, Capability Portfolio Managers, acquisition professionals, PAE MC Rapid Capability Cell (RCC) representatives, and Small Business experts will share information about emerging requirements, acquisition priorities, and anticipated contracting opportunities across the Marine Corps enterprise. And we don't want the conversation to go only one way. MCAX is also our opportunity to hear from you. What are you seeing in the marketplace? Where is technology moving? What capabilities already exist that we should know about? And where can better communication between Government and Industry help us find smarter ways to meet the needs of the warfighter? That exchange matters. Because when Government better understands what industry can deliver�and industry better understands where the Marine Corps is going�we can have better conversations about how to get there. Whether you've supported the Marine Corps for decades, you're an innovative small business looking for your first opportunity, or you're somewhere in between, you're invited to be part of that conversation. Come hear what we're working on. Ask questions. Engage with the people behind the requirements. And gain a clearer understanding of where your capabilities may align with what comes next. EVENT FORMAT We know your time is valuable. That's why we're continuing to focus MCAX on the information and engagement that industry has told us matters most. The approximately four-hour live event is anticipated to include: Briefs from leaders in Portfolio Acquisition Executive Marine Corps (PAE MC), Headquarters Marine Corps, Installations & Logistics (HQMC I&L), Portfolio Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS), PAE MC Cyber Technology Office, PAE MC RCC, and the Combat Development & Integration (CD&I) Capability Portfolio Managers (CPMs) Contract Opportunity Briefs from PAE MC, HQMC I&L and PAE MS Information Technology Contracting Center (ITCC) Industry Q&A We will continue streamlining formal presentations wherever possible so there is more time for meaningful engagement between Industry and Government. And because showing up prepared makes for a better conversation, we're giving you a head start. Before MCAX, take some time to explore the PAE MC Industry Portal at: https://www.pae.marines.mil/industry-portal/ The portal is designed to help industry learn more about PAE MC, our mission, and how to engage with us before the conversation begins. Have a capability we should know about? Industry partners are encouraged to submit capability briefs or white papers through the Industry Portal before the event. Sharing that information in advance gives our team an opportunity to better understand what you bring to the table and where your capabilities may connect with Marine Corps needs. A preview of selected contracting opportunities associated with the 19 November MCAX will also be added to this notice as soon as it becomes available. Industry partners are encouraged to check this notice periodically for updates prior to the event, review the opportunities in advance, and come ready to engage. HQMC I&L opportunities will be released to industry within five business days following the event through a separate SAM.gov announcement. One Mission. Many Opportunities. One Conversation Worth Having. We hope you'll join us on 19 November.

title: Maintenance Dredging of the Isle au Haut Thoroughfare near Isle au Haut, Maine
description: The Isle au Haut Thoroughfare Federal Navigation Project, located between Isle au Haut, Maine and Kimball Island, Maine on the outskirts of Penobscot Bay, about six miles southeast of Stonington and 25 miles east of Rockland. The Federal Navigation Project consists of a -6-foot Mean Lower Low Water (MLLW) deep by 75-foot wide extending 1,200-foot in length through the shoal in the thoroughfare.The proposed work consists of mechanically dredging approximately 3,355 cubic yards (cy) (1,183 cy required, plus 2,172 cy overdepth) of shoaled material consisting of highly compacted coarse sand and gravel, with areas of cobbles and isolated small boulders from the channel. Due to the material type, a mechanical dredge with the ability to dig highly compacted coarse sand and gravel will be required. The proposed action is to dredge to the authorized depth of -6-foot MLLW plus an additional 1-foot of required advance maintenance with an additional allowable 1-foot of overdepth (e.g. -7-foot MLLW required + 1-foot allowable OD). One-time, advanced maintenance is approved for the entirety of the 1200-foot long authorized channel. The dredged material will be placed at the Flake Island Disposal Site (FIDS) which is approximately 1 nautical mile northwest of the FNP. Placement of the dredged material (sand, gravel and cobble) at Flake Island Disposal Site will benefit both juvenile lobster habitat and juvenile cod by increasing the areas habitat complexity.The anticipated allowable dredging window is between September 15 and April 1 to avoid impacts to spawning shellfish, benthic resources, Essential Fish Habitat (EFH) of federally managed species, threatened and endangered species and interactions with mobile fishing gear.

description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotations are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 127EAX27Q0004 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for updates to the Grizzly Bear Campground. Updates include: Road alignment will be adjusted to accommodate expected traffic, subbase will be enhanced. The water system well will remain; the pumphouse, service and distribution lines, and point-of-use hydrants will be replaced and rerouted to better serve campers. The information board will be replaced and relocated. Host and Volunteer Sites will each to be equipped with sewage vault, water, and electric services. Campsites will be redesigned for accessibility and improved layout, parking and functionality. A new stick-built double toilet and stick-built pump house are part of the project. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 237990 The small business size standard is $45.0M This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will be considered by the agency.

title: Y1DA--VISN 2 EHRM Industry Day
description: Construction Industry Day Introduction In accordance with FAR Companion (FC) 10.001(c), this notice is for information and planning purposes only and is not to be construed as a solicitation or obligation on the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), nor will the VA pay for information requested. Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) will host an industry day event at the James J. Peters Department of Veterans Affairs VA Medical Center (VAMC), located at 130 West Kingsbridge Road, Bronx, NY 10468 for all businesses (including, but not limited to, general contractors, subcontractor trades, and material suppliers) interested in the upcoming Electronic Health Records Modernization (EHRM) Infrastructure Upgrades construction projects throughout VISN 2 (NY/NJ). The purpose of the Industry Day is to facilitate collaboration between the VA and general construction contractors and subcontractors of all business sizes who are interested in performing work in New York and New Jersey. This session is designed to give all interested contractors a clear understanding of the project s intent, performance expectations, and execution approach. This industry day will help the VA determine the method of procurement and type of socioeconomic set-aside, if any, highlight any industry concerns, gauge general contractor interest in the project, and perform a site walk to show key areas of the Bronx EHRM project. Six EHRM Infrastructure projects were solicited and awarded in FY26. Four of the six were designated as SDVOSB set-asides, and most of these projects received limited bids or proposals. In FY27, VISN 2 anticipates three projects, Bronx, Manhattan, and Northport, that are particularly large and complex, which may pose significant challenges for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs) to execute independently due to their scale and technical requirements. As a result, the VA is considering broadening the competition beyond SDVOSBs, seeking participation from both small and/or large businesses that have the project experience, capabilities, and workforce necessary to fulfill the contract demands. This approach is critical to ensuring a robust competitive environment that accurately reflects market value and supports successful project delivery. EVENT INFORMATION The industry day will be held on Thursday, November 19th, 2026, from 9:00 AM to 3:00 PM ET. The meeting location will be Room 3D-22 in Building 100, located at 130 West Kingsbridge Road, Bronx, NY 10468. Contractors are required to pre-register for this event. See Administrative section below. Proposed Agenda: 1. Check-in (please arrive between 9 - 9:30 AM) 2. Introductions 3. Meet and Greet 4. Overview of the EHRM Program and Each Project 4. Site walk of the Bronx VAMC EHRM project 5. Lunch Break 6. Questions and answers session 7. Networking *A final agenda will most likely be posted to SAM.gov closer to the event date. PROJECT DESCRIPTIONS VISN 2 (New York/New Jersey) has five EHRM projects that are anticipated to be solicited and awarded in Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 and four in FY 2028. The five planned locations for FY27 are at the following VAMC s: Bronx, Canandaigua, Manhattan, Northport, and St. Albans. A description of each project is listed below. Bronx VAMC: The design modernizes the campus technology backbone and supporting building systems so the medical center can implement the VA EHRM platform while maintaining reliable clinical and facility operations. Work extends across the Main Hospital (Building 100) and multiple adjacent campus buildings and support facilities. A distinguishing feature is the construction of two new telecommunications towers. The towers expand communications capacity and require coordinated architectural, structural, civil, electrical, mechanical, and telecommunications design. The broader project also renovates and expands existing telecommunications and data center spaces and upgrades the supporting power, cooling, fiber, security, and life-safety infrastructure. Canandaigua VAMC: This project comprehensively upgrades the campus s fiber optic network and power distribution systems to meet EHRM design guide requirements, ensuring robust support for clinical and facility operations. The work encompasses fiber network enhancements with redundant routes to each IT closet and the main demarcation room, minimizing risk through parallel systems operation during transitions from legacy to new infrastructure. The project also includes expansion or relocation of telecommunications rooms, installation of 100 new IT outlets and 75 electrical outlets, and substantial improvements in power distribution and HVAC systems. Enhanced physical security is provided through secure data cabinets, protected fiber infrastructure, secured telecommunications rooms, and installation of lockable manhole covers for underground fiber pathways. In addition, hazardous material abatement activities will ensure that all upgraded spaces meet current safety and environmental standards. Manhattan VAMC: The design modernizes telecommunications and IT infrastructure throughout Buildings 1, 2, 3, and 6 and creates resilient power and cooling systems to support continuous healthcare operations and future technology demands. The project relocates the existing data center to renovated space and upgrades 53 telecommunications rooms and enclosures. The new data center functions as the campus telecommunications hub and is supported by redundant fiber pathways, dedicated year-round cooling, and 2N UPS and electrical distribution redundancy. These features distinguish the Manhattan project and increase the reliability of critical IT systems. Northport VAMC: This information will be provided in an update to this posting on SAM.gov. St. Albans VAMC: The EHRM Infrastructure Upgrades Project at St. Albans VA Medical Center in Queens, NY, is a large-scale modernization effort designed to support the implementation of the VA s new EHRM system. The initiative involves major upgrades across multiple buildings, including the construction of a new data center and telecom tower, extensive electrical and mechanical improvements, and the installation of advanced technology infrastructure such as Cat 6A cabling and a fiber optic backbone, all guided by strict VA standards for compliance, safety, and scalability. Key challenges include managing hazardous materials like asbestos and lead-based paint, addressing spatial and technical constraints in existing telecom rooms, coordinating complex system upgrades within an active healthcare environment, and ensuring meticulous phasing to minimize disruptions. Additionally, the project must integrate diverse building systems, adhere to evolving standards, and provide future-proofing for anticipated growth, all of which add significant complexity to both the design and execution phases. *The following projects anticipated for award in FY28: Albany, Buffalo, Batavia and East Orange. Procurement Information The proposed projects will be a competitive firm-fixed-price contract utilizing the design-bid-build approach (final specifications and drawings will be provided). The anticipated solicitation will be issued as either request for proposals (RFP) in accordance with FAR part 15, considering technical and price factors or Invitation for Bids (IFBs) in accordance with FAR part 14, considering price only. The full acquisition strategy for this proposed project has not yet been developed and will be determined after the industry day and any additional market research is concluded. The targeted cost ranges of each project are listed below. Between $20 and $30 Million: Canandaigua and St. Albans Between $40 and $50 Million: Bronx and Manhattan Between $50 and $60 Million: Northport The applicable NAICS code for this requirement is 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction, with a small business size standard of $45 million. Countermeasures That Work (CMTW) Updates
description: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) maintains Countermeasures That Work, an evidence-based reference guide used by State Highway Safety Offices (SHSOs) and other stakeholders to identify effective behavioral traffic safety countermeasures. NHTSA is seeking contractor support to update the guide based on the latest available research, emerging countermeasures, and developments in highway safety. The purpose of this requirement is to update the current 12th edition of Countermeasures That Work and its electronic version (E-CMTW), resulting in the 13th edition. The contractor will conduct comprehensive literature searches, review and evaluate relevant research, and incorporate significant new findings, resources, and implementation considerations into approximately three to four program-area chapters annually. The final deliverable will include a consolidated Word document incorporating all updates made during the period of performance.

When any change in design, material, servicing or part number is made to replace or substitute any item to be furnished on this contract/purchase order, the Contractor shall furnish, for the substituting/replacement item, a drawing and an explanation of the reason for the change, explaining the reason therefor. If finished detail drawings are not available, shop drawings in the form used by the manufacturer will be acceptable for Government evaluation. When notifying the Procurement Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE ONLY - If the Manufacturer's Part Number indicated thereon has changed, but the parts are identical in all respects, supply the item and advise NAVICP-MECH immediately of the new part number. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. Code 4: Part redesigned - Old and new parts are completely interchangeable. Code 5: Part redesigned - New part replaces old. Old part cannot replace new. Code 6: Part redesigned - Parts not interchangeable. 3.4 Mercury Free - The material supplied under this contract/purchase order is intended for use on submarines/surface ships and therefore shall contain no metallic mercury and shall be free from mercury contamination. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor present in an unreplenished submarine/surface ship atmosphere. 4. QUALITY ASSURANCE 4.1 Responsibility for Inspection - Unless otherwise specified in the contract/purchase order, the Contractor is responsible for the performance of all inspection requirements as specified herein.

PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. SOLICITATION ANNOUNCEMENT: AN/BYG-1 APPLICATIONS The Department of the Navy, Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA), on behalf of the Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Undersea (PAE Undersea) and the Director, Submarine Programs (DSP), is releasing the formal solicitation for the AN/BYG-1 Applications requirement from the Submarine Combat and Weapons Control Program Office (PMS 425). This notice follows the previously published Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) and Industry Day event. The Government has reviewed the feedback received during and after the Industry Day and has revised the requirements accordingly for this final solicitation. SCOPE OF THE REQUIREMENT (GENERAL OVERVIEW) AN/BYG-1 is the U.S. Navy�s Submarine Combat Control System. The AN/BYG-1 provides tools for the analysis of surface, sub-surface, and airborne contacts operating in the vicinity of own-ship and within the mission theater. This analysis supports command and decision-making, payload and attack control functions, determination of ballistic data for legacy torpedoes, and initiation of firing sequence for all payload types in support of submarine mission areas. The scope of this solicitation encompasses the development, testing, integration, delivery, logistics, and full-lifecycle sustainment of compiled AN/BYG-1 software baselines. This includes current, future, and legacy AN/BYG-1 applications as part of a modernized capability delivery framework. Key objectives and technical efforts under this contract include: Deliver AN/BYG-1 capabilities and baselines in alignment with Submarine Tactical Requirements Group priorities Decouple AN/BYG-1 applications from hardware and software dependencies Implement microcontainer/microservices AN/BYG-1 architecture Transform AN/BYG-1 development and test environments by increasing virtualization and establishing a common, shared infrastructure Develop and integrate tactical decision aids that leverage artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies Assist with the design, development, and integration of combat control system elements to support international cooperative agreements and joint programs. description: Description NOTE: On 22 September 2026, Solicitation Amendment 002 was published in the E-TIC portal, including a revised solicitation, a revised Section L and other changes, all of which are identified in the Amendment summary of changes. The solicitation also extends the proposal due date to 5 November 2026 at 4:00 pm Eastern Standard Time. NOTE: On 8 August 2026, Solicitation Amendment 001 was published in the E-TIC portal, including a revised solicitation, a revised Section L, and a Question & Answer set Batch 1. SOLICITATION ANNOUNCEMENT: AN/BYG-1 APPLICATIONS The Department of the Navy, Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA), on behalf of the Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Undersea (PAE Undersea) and the Director, Submarine Programs (DSP), is releasing the formal solicitation for the AN/BYG-1 Applications requirement from the Submarine Combat and Weapons Control Program Office (PMS 425). This notice follows the previously published Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) and Industry Day event. The Government has reviewed the feedback received during and after the Industry Day and has revised the requirements accordingly for this final solicitation. SCOPE OF THE REQUIREMENT (GENERAL OVERVIEW) AN/BYG-1 is the U.S. Navy�s Submarine Combat Control System. The AN/BYG-1 provides tools for the analysis of surface, sub-surface, and airborne contacts operating in the vicinity of own-ship and within the mission theater. This analysis supports command and decision-making, payload and attack control functions, determination of ballistic data for legacy torpedoes, and initiation of firing sequence for all payload types in support of submarine mission areas. The scope of this solicitation encompasses the development, testing, integration, delivery, logistics, and full-lifecycle sustainment of compiled AN/BYG-1 software baselines. This includes current, future, and legacy AN/BYG-1 applications as part of a modernized capability delivery framework. Key objectives and technical efforts under this contract include: Deliver AN/BYG-1 capabilities and baselines in alignment with Submarine Tactical Requirements Group priorities Decouple AN/BYG-1 applications from hardware and software dependencies Implement microcontainer/microservices AN/BYG-1 architecture Transform AN/BYG-1 development and test environments by increasing virtualization and establishing a common, shared infrastructure Develop and integrate tactical decision aids that leverage artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies Assist with the design, development, and integration of combat control system elements to support international cooperative agreements and joint programs. ACCESS TO SOLICITATION DOCUMENTS AND CLASSIFIED DATA The AN/BYG-1 Applications solicitation, Statement of Work (SOW), and associated unclassified attachments are designated as Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and will not be posted directly to SAM.gov. These documents will be made available exclusively via the secure Electronic Technical Information Center (E-TIC) portal hosted by the Advanced Interactive Management Technology Center (AIMTC). Additionally, portions of the Government Furnished Information, specifically, the classified software source code provided to support proposal development are classified at the SECRET level and will be transmitted physically. Documents made available during this procurement may contain classified data and/or technical data whose export is restricted by the Arms Export Control Act. Foreign participation shall be limited by applicable legal authorities, regulations, and other security classification requirements as specified in the DD Form 254. Consolidated Access Request Instructions Prospective Offerors must submit a single, consolidated access request email to the Points of Contact listed below to obtain E-TIC portal access and the classified GFI software package. Email Attachments Required: DD Form 254: A completed copy of the DD Form 254. Block 6 must verify that the requesting company possesses a Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) issued SECRET facility clearance (FCL) and SECRET safeguarding capability. CRITICAL SECURITY NOTE FOR AWARD ELIGIBILITY: While a SECRET FCL is sufficient for proposal preparation and GFI access, the Offeror must ultimately possess a fully adjudicated TOP SECRET facility clearance and TOP SECRET safeguarding capability, issued by the U.S. Government, no later than contract award. The Government will not sponsor facility clearance upgrades or personnel clearance upgrades for the purpose of proposal submission or contract award eligibility. title: Facility Enhancement and Maintenance IDIQ
description: This requirement is for a non-personal services, Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract to provide all management, labor, materials, equipment, tools, transportation, and supervision necessary for facility enhancement and maintenance at Joint Base Lindsey Graham, South Carolina, and its associated locations. Auf dem Grundstück sind die folgenden Neubaumaßnahmen geplant: 1) Zubau Hamburger Schulhaus (angelehnt an das Hamburger Klassenhaus) und 2) Zubau Zweifeldhalle. Gegenstand der vorliegenden GU-Ausschreibung ist der Zubau des Hamburger Schulhauses in Anlehnung an das Hamburger Klassenhaus. Die Realisierung erfolgt über einen Generalunternehmer, der die LPH 5-8 erbringt und das Gebäude in vorgefertigter Bauweise erstellt. Das bestehende Schulgelände umfasst einen Gebäudebestand von 6 Gebäuden unterschiedlicher Gebäudeklassen inkl. einer bestehenden und an das Baufeld angrenzenden mobilen Klassenraumanlage. Letztere verbleibt bis zur Fertigstellung des Hamburger Schulhauses im Betrieb. Das Grundstück weist eine Gesamtfläche von ca. 20.861 m² auf. Für die Schule ist eine 5-Zügigkeit geplant. Im dreigeschossigen Gebäude, mit einer BGF in Höhe von ca. 2.019 m² und einer Mietfläche (NRF) in Höhe von ca. 1.729 m², werden im EG ein Foyer, eine Essenseinnahmefläche, eine Vitalküche für 300-600 VT, eine kleine Multifunktionsfläche und sonstige Nebenflächen vorgesehen. Im 1.OG werden 3 geschlossene Klassenräume, 2 geschlossene Lernstudios, 1 offene Multifunktionsfläche, 1 „Maker Hub“ mit Podcaststudio, 1 Bibliothek, 1 Teeküche, Garderobenflächen und sonstige Nebenflächen vorgesehen. Im 2.OG werden 3 geschlossene Klassenräume, 2 geschlossene Lernstudios, 1 offene Multifunktionsfläche, 1 Handarbeits-/ Handwerksfläche inkl. Lernstützpunkt, 1 Kunstatelier und sonstige Nebenflächen vorgesehen. --------------- Hier: GU-Leistung --------------- Schlüsselfertige Erstellung eines Neubaus

title: Denmark – Financial consultancy services – Rammeaftale på økonomikonsulenter - 26/17294
description: Den udbudte ydelse omfatter opgaver vedrørende løbende økonomisk assistance, som primært skal udføres i Energinet Koncernen, der omfatter et Shared servicecenter med økonomiydelser, indkøbssupport samt en økonomifunktion med drifts- og anlægscontrolling og -analyse. Derudover kan der i koncernens moderselskab samt øvrige datterselskaber være behov for løbende økonomisk assistance primært i form af finansiel controlling samt andre økonomirelaterede ad-hoc opgaver. De udbudte ydelser omfatter ikke den lovpligtige finansielle revision af Ordregiver og tilhørende datterselskaber. Ydelserne må ikke konflikte med de lovgivningsmæssige begrænsninger, der er i ydelser fra revisionsvirksomheder. Omtalte rammeaftale vil dog følge Ordregivers aftale ved lovpligtig finansiel revision. For yderligere detaljer vedrørende anskaffelsen henvises til de tilhørende bilag. Den udbudte rammeaftale har en løbetid på 4 år. Rammeaftalen kan forlænges i 2 år af 2 omgange, svarende til 4+2+2 år. Rammeaftalens samlede værdi forventes at udgøre 64.000.000 kr. Forbruget kan alene anses som et estimat, og er som følge heraf ikke forpligtende for Ordregiver. Ordregiver har ret, men ikke pligt, til at købe de af rammeaftalen omfattede ydelser hos den valgte tilbudsgiver, jf. rammeaftalens pkt. 1.3

title: Germany – Photographic services – Bildbeurteilung und -bearbeitung für die eGK
description: Die Techniker Krankenkasse (TK) gibt gem. § 291 SGB V für jeden Versicherten eine elektronische Gesundheitskarte (eGK) aus. Die eGK dient als Nachweis zur Inanspruchnahme von Leistungen im Rahmen der vertragsärztlichen Versorgung und ist für Versicherte ab 15 Jahren grundsätzlich mit einem Bild des Karteninhabers auszustatten. Aus diesem Grund fordert die TK bei ihren Kunden ein Bild an. Die angeforderten Bilder können auf dem Postweg eingereicht oder online hochgeladen werden. Die bei der TK eingereichten Bilder werden, so diese nicht online hochgeladen wurden, im ersten Schritt von der TK digitalisiert. Die weitere Bildbeurteilung und -bearbeitung nimmt die TK nicht selbst vor, sondern beauftragt hierfür den Auftragnehmer (AN). Dieser prüft, beurteilt und bearbeitet die Fotos zu eGK-spezifikationskonformen Bildern für die Produktion der eGK.

title: Germany – Energy and related services – 10012448-Accord-cadre sur la transition énergétique - Pool Experts en appui au PEDIII
description: The "Sustainable Energy Programme in Senegal" (PED III) is a technical cooperation project of the Senegalese Ministry of Energy, Oil and Mines (MEPM), financed by BMZ and implemented by GIZ. The project amounts to 7.500.000 EUR and runs from 01/2026 to 12/2028. The main implementing partners are, besides the MEPM, the Agence pour l'économie et la gestion de l'énergie (AEME), the Agence nationale des énergies renouvelables (ANER), the Agence sénégalaise de l'électrification rurale (ASER), the Commission de régulation du secteur de l'électricité (CRSE), the Compagnie nationale de l'électricité (SENELEC), the private sector and civil society. The aim of PED III is "to support the effective implementation of the Just Energy Transition by the main players in Senegal's public and private sectors at both strategic and operational levels". The project contributes to achieving the objectives of the national energy policy linked to renewable energy (RE) and energy efficiency (EE) for the implementation of the 2030 Agenda SDGs, in particular SDG 7 (access to energy), 8 (decent work and economic growth), 9 (industrialisation) and 13 (combating climate change), as well as German support for achieving the objectives of the Just Energy Transition Partnership (JET-P) signed between Senegal and the G7 in June 2023. The project's target groups are the public sector (ministries, national and decentralised authorities, training and research establishments) and the private sector (media, businesses, private sector support structures and women's socio-economic organisations). The Senegalese population will have greater access to a competitive and sustainable energy supply. New jobs linked to the fair energy transition are within the reach of women, young people and professionals, depending on their areas of expertise. At national level, the capacities of the Ministry of Energy and other stakeholders to steer the energy transition process will be strengthened. In addition, support for the operationalisation of the ecosystem enabling private investment in the transition will be supported. Lastly, the economic opportunities of the transition and the capacity-building required for its deployment will be promoted. The expected results of the project are as follows: 1. The coherent governance structure for RE & EE within JETP is strengthened. 2. The framework conditions for the integration of renewable energies into the grid and private investment in renewable energies and energy efficiency are improved 3. Public and private players have the necessary skills to implement inclusive energy transition projects.

title: Germany – Shelves – Rahmenvertrag über die Lieferung inklusive Montage von Schülerfächerschränken, Stahlschränken und Schwerlastregalen für die Schulen in Trägerschaft der Stadt Essen
description: Für den laufenden Betrieb der Essener Schulen werden unterjährig regelmäßig verschiedene Schränke benötigt, dessen Lieferung Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung ist. Die Leistung soll in Form eines Rahmenvertrags vergeben werden. Der Auftragnehmer ist verpflichtet, das beauftragte Mobiliar innerhalb einer Frist von maximal 48 Werktagen nach Abruf frei Verwendungsstelle an die verschiedenen Schulen im Essener Stadtgebiet zu liefern. Der Vertrag beginnt mit Zuschlagserteilung, voraussichtlich am 04.01.2027. Die Grundvertragslaufzeit beträgt zwei Jahre, mit der Option auf einmalige Verlängerung um zwei weitere Jahre, sodass die maximale Laufzeit vier Jahre beträgt. Der Auftragnehmer hält sich während der vereinbarten Grundvertragslaufzeit an die von ihm angebotenen Festpreise gebunden (Festpreisbindung). Nach Ablauf dieser Bindefrist ist der Auftragnehmer berechtigt, für die verbleibende Restvertragslaufzeit ein schriftliches Preisanpassungsverlangen zu stellen. Das Entstehen sowie die Höhe des Preisanpassungsanspruchs bemessen sich nach der Entwicklung des Erzeugerpreisindexes gewerblicher Produkte (Deutschland, Monate, Güterverzeichnis [GP20192-/3-/4-/5-/6-/9-Steller/ Sonderpositionen] ), veröffentlicht vom Statistischen Bundesamt in der Datenbank GENESIS-Online (Tabelle: "Erzeugerpreisindex gewerblicher Produkte"). Für Los 1 (Schülerfächerschränke): GP19-31 Möbel Für Los 2 und 3 (Stahlschränke und Schwerlastregale): GP19-25 Metallerzeugnisse Eine Preisanpassung ist möglich, sofern in den ersten 18 Monaten der Vertragslaufzeit eine durchschnittliche Preissteigerung/Preissenkung von über 5% entstanden ist. Der Antrag auf eine Preissteigerung ist der Auftraggeberin zwei Monate vor Ablauf der Bindefrist seitens des Auftragnehmers vorzulegen. Umgekehrt ist die Preissenkung zwei Monate vor Ablauf der Bindefrist von der Auftraggeberin gegenüber dem Auftragnehmer geltend zu machen. Nach Ablauf der Grundvertragslaufzeit und erfolgter Antragstellung werden die Preise dann für die Restvertragslaufzeit auf Grundlage der oben genannten Preisindizes neu ermittelt. Anerkannt wird dabei lediglich die den Fünf-Prozent-Satz übersteigende Preissteigerung/-senkung. Eine Kündigung des Vertrags durch die Auftraggeberin nach Ablauf der Grundvertragslaufzeit ist möglich. Sofern bis zu einem Zeitpunkt von drei Monaten vor der jeweiligen Beendigung der Vertragslaufzeit keine Kündigung des Vertrags seitens der Stadt Essen erfolgt ist, verlängert sich der Vertrag stillschweigend um zwei weitere Jahre. Sollte der Gesamtauftragswert für die Maximallaufzeit von vier Jahren früher ausgeschöpft sein, endet der Vertrag zum Zeitpunkt der vollständigen Ausschöpfung. Der Auftragnehmer hat eine Garantie von 5 Jahren auf das gesamte Mobiliar zu gewähren.

Eftersom Ekeröledens affärsmodell bygger på användaravgifter kommer även en liten minskning av resandeunderlaget resultera i att intäkterna inte längre kan täcka kostnaderna.
